triage.name: Scurvy
triage.reason: Dietary vitamin C deficiency with gingival bleeding, perifollicular hemorrhage and poor wound healing; classic history-plus-exam diagnosis.

review_issues: exam: term 'Abnormal hair' not found in SNOMED CT
exam: term 'Tenderness of calf' not found in SNOMED CT

demographics: Seen in people with severely restricted diets, food insecurity, or alcohol use disorder
More common in older adults living alone or in institutions
Can occur in children with restrictive eating patterns or developmental conditions

risk_factors.text: Diet lacking fresh fruits and vegetables for months
Living alone or in an institution with limited diet variety
Dialysis or chronic illness with poor intake

social_history: Lives alone or in a care facility

chief_complaints.text: My gums bleed when I brush my teeth
I feel weak and tired all the time
I have red spots on my legs
My legs hurt and feel tight

hpi.duration: Usually 1–3 months of poor dietary intake before symptoms appear
hpi.progression: Starts with fatigue and poor appetite, then bleeding gums, easy bruising, and leg pain develop; wounds heal slowly and old scars may break down
hpi.radiation: Leg pain may radiate to the thighs
hpi.quality: Gums are sore and spongy; leg pain is aching and tight; skin spots are flat and red

atypical.how_it_differs: Infants present with irritability, poor feeding, and pseudoparalysis (refusal to move a limb) rather than gum bleeding.
Older adults may have fewer gum findings if edentulous, and present with weakness, easy bruising, and leg swelling.
Children may present with bone pain, limping, and poor growth rather than classic skin and gum findings.

general.mild: Tired but not ill-appearing; favors the legs when walking
general.moderate: Pale, listless, walks slowly with a limp or stiff-legged gait
general.severe: Ill-appearing, pale, reluctant to stand or walk, holds the legs
general.critical: Toxic-appearing, pale, weak, unable to bear weight or move the affected limb

findings.maneuver: Inspect the gums and gently press or brush along the gingival margin
findings.finding: Bleeding from the gum margins, especially between teeth
Swollen, spongy, friable gums that are bluish-purple and bleed easily

findings.maneuver: Gently press on the teeth or ask the patient to wiggle them
findings.finding: Teeth are loose in their sockets

findings.maneuver: Inspect the skin of the legs and arms with good lighting, looking at hair follicles
findings.finding: Pinpoint hemorrhages around hair follicles, often with broken or coiled hairs

findings.maneuver: Inspect the lower legs and dependent areas
Inspect the skin for bruises, including areas of minor trauma
findings.finding: Easy bruising or large ecchymoses out of proportion to trauma

findings.maneuver: Inspect any wounds or old scars
findings.finding: Wounds healing slowly or old scars breaking down

findings.maneuver: Inspect body hair on the legs and arms
findings.finding: Hairs that are coiled or broken (corkscrew hairs)

findings.maneuver: Press over the shins and calves
findings.finding: Pitting edema of the lower legs
Tenderness and a brawny, woody feel to the muscles of the calves and thighs

findings.maneuver: Palpate the knees, ankles and other joints and move them through range of motion
findings.finding: Joint tenderness, and sometimes warmth or swelling, without deformity

findings.maneuver: Inspect and palpate a painful joint
findings.finding: Blood within the joint space causing swelling and restricted movement

findings.maneuver: Inspect the conjunctivae, palms and mucous membranes
findings.finding: Pallor of the conjunctivae and skin

findings.maneuver: Measure the temperature and assess for systemic signs
Palpate the left upper quadrant and percuss for splenic dullness
Palpate the cervical, axillary and inguinal lymph node chains
Pinch and inspect the skin of the hands and face
findings.finding: No thickening or tightening of the skin

findings.maneuver: Inspect and move the joints of the hands, knees and ankles

labs.caveat: Anemia is usually normocytic or mildly macrocytic; it can be multifactorial when diet is generally poor.
Mild macrocytosis can occur; marked macrocytosis should prompt checking B12 and folate.
Mild thrombocytopenia can occur; bleeding is mainly due to defective collagen and capillary fragility, not low platelets.
Usually normal or only mildly elevated; a high value suggests another process such as infection.
Low when overall nutrition is poor.
Check because a poor diet often causes multiple deficiencies; low B12 changes the anemia workup.
Check alongside B12 in restricted diets.
Coagulation studies are usually normal; mild prolongation may reflect poor nutrition or liver disease.
Usually normal; abnormal values point to another bleeding disorder.

imaging.preferred_when: Only when another cause of the bleeding or malabsorption is suspected

findings.text: Gastric or duodenal erosions from a separate process

imaging.preferred_when: Only for focal neurologic deficits or suspected intracranial bleeding

findings.text: No acute abnormality in most patients

initial.why: Anemia, thrombocytopenia and other cytopenias; helps exclude leukemia and marrow disease
Baseline electrolytes and renal function, especially with poor intake or alcohol use
Albumin and liver tests to assess overall nutritional and hepatic status
Screens for a coagulation disorder as an alternative cause of bleeding
Screens for a coagulation disorder as an alternative cause of bleeding
Nonspecific inflammation marker; helps frame an alternative systemic illness
Helps exclude an infectious or inflammatory process

confirmatory.why: Low level confirms vitamin C deficiency; the decisive test when the history and exam suggest scurvy

supporting.why: Common coexisting deficiency in restricted diets
Common coexisting deficiency in restricted diets
Iron deficiency can coexist and contribute to the anemia
Part of the anemia evaluation when iron deficiency is suspected
Helps interpret iron status in a patient with anemia

not_indicated.why: No role in the evaluation of nutritional bleeding; a positive result would only mislead
Not routine; reserve for suspected gastrointestinal bleeding or malabsorption
not_indicated.only_if: there is evidence of gastrointestinal bleeding or malabsorption

not_indicated.why: Not routine; only for focal neurologic findings or suspected intracranial hemorrhage
not_indicated.only_if: focal neurologic deficits or suspected intracranial bleeding

not_indicated.why: Not routine; consider only if myeloma is suspected from hypercalcemia, renal failure, bone lesions or a markedly elevated total protein

decision_points: Confirm the diagnosis with a serum ascorbic acid level before attributing bleeding to scurvy
Check B12, folate and iron when the diet is broadly poor, since deficiencies often coexist
A normal platelet count and coagulation studies with bleeding gums and perifollicular hemorrhage point toward a collagen/vitamin C problem rather than a platelet or clotting disorder
Consider myeloma or a marrow disorder if there is hypercalcemia, renal impairment, bone pain or pancytopenia

differential.name: Immune thrombocytopenia
differential.why_considered: Petechiae, easy bruising and gum bleeding in a patient with a bleeding tendency
differential.trigger: Isolated low platelets with bleeding and no dietary history

history: Sudden onset of bruising and petechiae
Recent viral illness or new medication
exam: Petechiae and ecchymoses without gum hypertrophy
labs: Isolated thrombocytopenia with normal hemoglobin and white count

differential.name: Acute leukemia
differential.why_considered: Bleeding gums, bruising, fatigue and anemia in a patient who looks unwell
differential.trigger: Pancytopenia, blasts on smear, or lymphadenopathy and splenomegaly

history: Weeks of fatigue, fever, night sweats
exam: Gum infiltration rather than simple bleeding
imaging: Mediastinal mass or organomegaly on chest radiograph or CT

differential.name: Ehlers-Danlos syndrome
differential.why_considered: Easy bruising, poor wound healing and bleeding from fragile connective tissue

history: Lifelong easy bruising and poor scarring
exam: No gum bleeding or perifollicular hemorrhage
labs: Normal platelet count and coagulation studies
imaging: No specific imaging findings; genetic testing confirms the subtype

differential.name: Multiple myeloma
differential.why_considered: Anemia, bone pain and bleeding tendency in an older adult

history: Bone pain, especially back or ribs
labs: Elevated total protein with monoclonal spike on serum protein electrophoresis
imaging: Lytic bone lesions on skeletal survey or low-dose CT

differential.name: Vasculitis
differential.why_considered: Palpable purpura, joint pain and systemic symptoms

imaging: Chest imaging may show nodules or infiltrates; biopsy of affected tissue shows vessel inflammation

differential.name: Vitamin K deficiency or coagulopathy
differential.why_considered: Bleeding gums and easy bruising from a clotting problem

history: Antibiotic use, poor intake, or liver disease
exam: No spongy gums or corkscrew hairs
labs: Low vitamin K level if measured

severity.mild: Fatigue, poor appetite, and early gum tenderness or bleeding with brushing; no significant anemia or functional limitation
severity.moderate: Established disease with spongy bleeding gums, perifollicular hemorrhage, easy bruising, leg pain and mild anemia; some limitation in walking or daily activities
severity.severe: Marked gingival bleeding and loose teeth, extensive ecchymoses, brawny leg edema, joint pain, significant anemia, and poor wound healing; patient is reluctant to walk
severity.critical: Rare life-threatening presentation with severe anemia, hypotension, or bleeding into a critical site such as the central nervous system or pericardium

red_flags.finding: Syncope, dyspnea at rest, or heart rate over 120 with pallor
red_flags.meaning: Severe anemia from chronic blood loss or poor erythropoiesis; needs urgent transfusion assessment
Hemodynamic instability, possibly from occult hemorrhage or sepsis; resuscitate and investigate urgently

red_flags.finding: Focal neurologic deficit, severe headache, or new confusion
red_flags.meaning: Possible intracranial hemorrhage; obtain urgent neuroimaging

red_flags.finding: Fever with purulent gums or spreading facial swelling
red_flags.meaning: Secondary infection of friable gingiva or periodontal tissue; needs antibiotics and dental evaluation

red_flags.finding: Rapidly enlarging bruise or swelling in a limb with pain and pallor
red_flags.meaning: Large soft-tissue or intramuscular hemorrhage; assess for compartment syndrome

complications.name: Secondary infection of gingiva or periodontal tissue
Poor wound healing and wound dehiscence
clues: Surgical or traumatic wound that fails to close

special_populations.differences: Present with irritability, poor feeding, and pseudoparalysis (refusal to move a limb) from subperiosteal hemorrhage; gum findings are absent because teeth have not erupted.
May present with bone pain, limp, and poor growth rather than classic skin and gum findings; consider in children with restrictive eating patterns or developmental conditions.
May have fewer gum findings if edentulous; present with weakness, easy bruising, leg swelling, and poor wound healing; often live alone or in institutions with limited diet variety.
Vitamin C requirements increase; deficiency can contribute to anemia and poor wound healing, and severe deficiency has been linked to adverse pregnancy outcomes.
Patients on dialysis lose vitamin C during treatment and may have restricted diets; maintain a higher index of suspicion.
Poor wound healing and friable gums may be more pronounced; secondary infection risk is higher.

key_questions.question: What have you been eating over the past few months? Do you eat any fresh fruits or vegetables?
key_questions.looking_for: A diet with no fresh fruits or vegetables for weeks to months; the single most important piece of history

key_questions.question: How long has it been since you ate fruit or vegetables?
key_questions.looking_for: Typically 1–3 months of severely restricted intake before symptoms appear

key_questions.question: Do your gums bleed when you brush your teeth or eat?
key_questions.looking_for: Bleeding from the gum margins, often the first thing the patient notices

key_questions.question: Have you noticed red or purple spots on your legs, or bruising more easily than usual?
key_questions.looking_for: Perifollicular hemorrhage, petechiae and easy bruising

key_questions.question: Do your legs hurt or feel tight? Does it hurt to walk?
key_questions.looking_for: Aching leg pain with a brawny, woody feel to the calves and thighs

key_questions.question: Have your teeth felt loose or has your gum felt swollen and spongy?
key_questions.looking_for: Loose teeth and spongy, friable gums in more advanced disease

key_questions.question: How have your energy and appetite been?
key_questions.looking_for: Fatigue and poor appetite, often the earliest symptoms

key_questions.question: Do you drink alcohol? How much and how often?
key_questions.looking_for: Alcohol use disorder, a strong risk factor for a diet devoid of fresh produce

key_questions.question: Who does your grocery shopping and cooking? Do you have trouble affording or getting fresh food?
key_questions.looking_for: Food insecurity, living alone, or institutional food with limited variety

key_questions.question: Have you had stomach or intestinal surgery, or been told you have trouble absorbing nutrients?
key_questions.looking_for: Bariatric surgery, celiac disease or other malabsorption

key_questions.question: Are you on dialysis or do you have chronic kidney disease?
key_questions.looking_for: Dialysis, which removes vitamin C and often comes with a restricted diet

key_questions.question: Have you had any fevers, weight loss or night sweats?
key_questions.looking_for: Absent; their presence points toward infection, malignancy or vasculitis instead

key_questions.question: Does anyone in your family have a bleeding or clotting problem?
key_questions.looking_for: Absent; a family history suggests an inherited bleeding disorder

key_questions.question: Have you had any recent trauma, or bleeding from the nose, gut or urine?
key_questions.looking_for: Trauma or bleeding from other sites, which changes the differential and urgency

key_questions.question: Are you taking any blood thinners or new medications?
key_questions.looking_for: Anticoagulants or antiplatelets that would explain the bleeding

reasoning_points: A diet lacking fresh fruits and vegetables for weeks to months, often with alcohol use disorder, food insecurity, living alone or malabsorption
Bleeding gums and spongy, friable gingiva, sometimes with loose teeth
Perifollicular hemorrhage, petechiae and easy bruising on the legs
Leg pain with a brawny, woody feel to the calves and thighs, and joint pain
Fatigue, poor appetite, pallor and a normocytic or mildly macrocytic anemia
Poor wound healing or breakdown of old scars
A normal platelet count and normal coagulation studies, which argue against a platelet or clotting disorder
A low serum ascorbic acid level confirming the diagnosis
Coexisting deficiencies such as B12, folate or iron considered when the diet is broadly poor
Look-alikes such as immune thrombocytopenia, leukemia, Ehlers-Danlos syndrome, myeloma and vasculitis excluded by the dietary history, exam and labs

easy: Older adult living alone or with alcohol use disorder who eats almost no fresh produce
Classic bleeding gums with perifollicular hemorrhage on the legs
Leg pain with a brawny, woody feel to the calves
Normal platelet count and coagulation studies
medium: Patient with fatigue and anemia but no obvious gum bleeding until asked directly
Edentulous older adult with weakness, easy bruising and leg swelling but no gum findings
Diet history only obtained after the student asks specifically about fruit and vegetables
Coexisting B12, folate or iron deficiency muddying the anemia picture
hard: Infant with irritability, poor feeding and pseudoparalysis rather than gum or skin findings
Child with bone pain, limp and poor growth rather than classic skin and gum findings
Patient on dialysis with a restricted diet and a high index of suspicion needed
Patient with a coexisting bleeding disorder or thrombocytopenia where scurvy is not the only explanation
Presentation with poor wound healing or a dehisced surgical wound and no bleeding complaints
